items.context: @matttttt187 (130.893 seguidores), en inglés: "Coinkite says a COLDCARD bug let attackers drain about $107M in BTC. Weak randomness since 2021. Cold storage was cold for everyone… Go make new seeds, fam" (con imagen). Noticia de ~38 min con 0 respuestas y 547 vistas. Custodia: se aporta por qué la actualización de firmware no salva una semilla afectada y la importancia de verificar la entropía.
items.suggested_text:
The part worth underlining: a firmware update doesn't save an affected seed. If the entropy was weak when it was created, the key was effectively predictable from day one, so the only fix is a new seed and an on-chain move of every coin to it. The reported count is 1,778.84 $BTC taken from 8,600+ addresses, and Coinkite says the flaw slipped past at least 15 reviews.

The uncomfortable lesson is that "cold" describes where a key lives, not how it was born. Rolling dice, or at least verifying the entropy yourself, removes the one step every other layer silently depends on. I put together how to build that kind of setup end to end: https://x.com/ForecastQuant/status/2123585216740528526

And a new seed only moves the question one level down: who, or what, generates the next one?
